body:
Slurm workers are launched with a blocking `srun`, so a worker is a step inside the driver's allocation rather than a job of its own, and its job id is never read. PBS ids are read from qsub and discarded. That leaves nothing to tie a worker to its allocation, which #360 needs for a worker registry.

This PR makes each worker its own batch job and keeps the id:

- `SlurmManager.launch` now submits with `sbatch --parsable` instead of `srun`, so `SlurmManager` allocations no longer nest, matching existing `PBSManager` behavior. The job id is parsed from stdout and stored in `WorkerConfig.userdata`.
- The startup poll no longer watches an `srun` process. It asks `squeue` or `qstat` every 30 s about jobs still waited on and skips any that left the queue before connecting. A submission the scheduler rejects is reported from its own error message.
- `sbatch` inherits SLURM_* from an enclosing allocation, so the submission environment strips them, reusing the list from the HPC backend.
- Fixes a bug in how the submission environment was built. deepcopy(ENV) returns ENV itself, since EnvDict has no fields to copy, so the delete! calls meant to strip SLURM_* from a copy were removing them from the driver process. Dict{String, String}(ENV) makes a real copy. This didn't really matter when only submit_job did it, but the worker path now does it on every add_workers.
title: Make each worker its own batch job, store job ID per worker
